summary: Iteration 3 — Project visibility filtering, per-project roles, and Team/Member Detail features. Backend: 70/70 pytest cases pass (49 existing regressions + 21 new for iteration 3). Verified: (a) viewer@demo.com sees ONLY Skyline in /projects, engineer sees BOTH, admin sees ALL; (b) my_roles field present per card, admin returns ['admin'], engineer contains 'site_engineer', viewer contains 'viewer'; (c) GET /projects/{green_id} as viewer returns 403; GET /projects/{skyline_id} returns 200 with my_role='viewer'; (d) Project members CRUD works — GET returns 3 members for Skyline, POST assigns with multi-roles, duplicate returns 409, PATCH updates roles, DELETE removes; (e) DELETE on the PM user returns 400 with the expected error message; (f) /organizations/current/members exposes projects_count, open_tasks_count, last_login_at; PM has projects_count≥2 (PM of both), viewer has =1 (Skyline only); (g) /organizations/current/members/{user_id} returns the shape {user, membership, projects[], task_stats(todo/in_progress/done/total/open), open_issues, recent_activity}; viewer detail shows only 1 project (Skyline) with role='viewer'; (h) RBAC — viewer cannot POST tasks on Skyline (403), engineer can, viewer 403 on Green Fields (non-member), PM can PATCH project, engineer cannot. Frontend: Playwright verified — viewer sees exactly 1 project card with 'YOUR ROLE: VIEWER' chip; Team page has search/role-filter/sort dropdowns + 9 clickable rows; MemberDetail shows all 5 stat cards + assigned-project list; Admin project detail Members tab renders with Assign Member button opening a modal that has 4 role-pick chips (admin/PM/site_engineer/viewer). All data-testids match the contract.

minor.issue: For an org admin, 'projects' list only includes projects where they are project_manager or explicit project_member — not all projects in the org. This can look inconsistent with 'admin sees all' from /projects. Consider clarifying: 'projects_count' on the member row already reflects only assignments (not visibility), and MemberDetail follows the same convention. Non-blocking.

When PM is stored implicitly (no project_members row), the returned row has id=null. Frontend still shows a pencil (edit-roles) for that row because the check keys off is_project_manager rather than id!=null; clicking edit would fail server-side (404) since no project_members row exists. Recommend hiding pencil when member.id is null, or auto-creating a project_members row on PM change. Frontend cosmetic edge.

ui_bugs.issue: For implicit-PM row (no project_members doc), an edit-roles pencil is still shown; clicking it will hit a 404 PATCH. Guard by member.id!=null.

action_items: OPTIONAL: In ProjectDetail Members panel, only show the edit-roles pencil when member.id is not null (implicit-PM rows have id=null and PATCH would 404). Alternatively, auto-create a project_members row for the PM on project create/patch.

OPTIONAL: Consider whether MemberDetail 'Projects assigned' for org admins should reflect all projects (they see them all) vs only assigned. Current: only assigned. This matches org member semantics but can confuse admins who see all projects on /projects. Doc it.
critical_code_review_comments: projects.py list_projects — visibility filter is correct; get_accessible_project_ids returns None for admin (bypass) and union of project_members+PM otherwise. Good.

deps.resolve_project_access — good: 404 when project not found (not 403) prevents leaking existence to non-members; but for a member without any role, 403 with detail 'You do not have access to this project.' — matches spec.
projects.py assign_project_member — 409 on duplicate is correct; consider allowing an idempotent upsert (merge roles) as an option later.

orgs.py list_members — computes projects_count using union of project_members and implicit PM rows; correct. But if a user was BOTH the PM and had a project_members row, count is deduped via set — good.

orgs.py get_member_detail — combines pm_docs + PM projects; roles_by_project only pulls from pm_docs, then adds 'project_manager' via is_pm flag. Note: if a project_members row already contains 'project_manager', we correctly avoid duplicate via the 'not in roles' guard.
ProjectDetail MembersPanel — pencil visible on implicit-PM row (id=null) leads to a 404 on PATCH. Minor UX bug; guard on member.id.
server.py migrate_project_members — runs at startup and backfills from projects.project_manager_id. Good idempotent migration.
